title: Mentioning the specific number of children predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention a lack of formal education may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who use strong character-based adjectives like 'resilient' or 'courageous' may fund faster.
Female borrowers requesting funds for non-business assets, such as sanitary toilets, may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention a specific future dream or community goal may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention personal hardships like being widowed or living in refugee camps may fund more slowly.
Gratitude may accelerate funding for men while slowing it for women.
Direct appeals for support from lenders may slow funding for both genders.
Female borrowers who include explicit expressions of gratitude to lenders fund more slowly.
Male borrowers who describe long-term dreams or business expansion goals may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention a history of successful loans from NWTF fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning a history of successful loan repayments has opposite effects on funding speed by gender.
